assertion_analysis: The _publish roundtrip assertion fails if persistence changes or drops its timestamp; it establishes fixture integrity rather than proving notice behavior.
The fixture-row assertion is a positive control: it fails if the real StationSubscriber.wake loop cannot deliver the known row.

Literal [producer-lost, producer-restored] and [0, 2*SAMPLE] assertions fail if polling or either transition is removed, delivery is delayed, or extra notices escape suppression; the recorded mutation fails the sequence assertion in all three modes.

Project, session, age and bound assertions fail if notice fields are missing or miscomputed; remedy equality verifies wiring to the established owner, while line membership fails if the project, age or remedy is omitted from the sentence.
The recovery project/zero-age/sentence checks fail if restoration reports stale data or drops project identity.
The continuing-loss [0, BOUND] assertion fails if throttling is removed or the repeat deadline is changed.
Fresh and exact-bound snapshots must leave only the literal fixture row: >= instead of > or unconditional loss emission fails this assertion.

CLI exit/stdout/stderr checks fail if new event kinds are refused, their sentences are dropped, or output goes to stderr; comparing supplied event text to captured stdout is a real renderer boundary check, not evidence that the producer generated that event.
The quiet-station reader assertion verifies its fresh heartbeat; the following fixture-row-only assertion fails if publication age is taken from the old payload instead.
The missing-publication fixture-row-only assertion fails if an absent timestamp invents loss or recovery.
The stale-export assertion confirms its setup; the literal loss/restoration sequence fails when the fresh session-snapshot fallback is removed.
The exhaustion empty-list assertion fails on unexpected output; reinstating unconditional subscriber continuation spins and fails the two-second timeout.
assertion_independence: No vacuous assertion found; persistence and renderer input-to-output checks have concrete failure modes, and literal event sequences and independent clock times protect the actual regression.
